The material facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, as have been stated in the instant revisional application, in short, are that the present petitioner as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No.129 of 2008 (Pre-emption) under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (Hereinafter referred as said Act) against the opposite parties in the Court of the Joint District Judge, Court No.1, Rajshahi for pre-emption of the case land. 

 6. Mr Abddul Jabbar, the learned Advocate has appeared for the petitioner and submitted that he has taken 3 grounds and today at the time of hearing of the Rule he also filed a supplementary affidavit in Court stating additional grounds. He also submitted that the Court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that the pre-emption case does not come within the purview of the plaint as contemplated under Order VII, rule 11 of the said Code, because it is a miscellaneous proceeding but not a suit. In the aforesaid miscellaneous proceeding the Court will not draw any decree which contemplated in sub- section (2) of Section 2 of the said Code, hence, the Court below has committed a gross error in law in rejecting the miscellaneous case. He has further submitted that on a plain reading of the application filed under Section 96 of the said Act, the cause of action apparent on the face of the record thus, the rejection of the plaint by the Court below on considering the external materials which have been stated in the application for rejection of the miscellaneous case under Order VII, rule 11 of the said Code is not only misconception of law within the ambit of Order VII, rule 11 of the said Code, rather the Court below committed serious error of law in deciding and allowing the said application. Therefore, it is liable to be set-aside. He has further submitted that the Court below in deciding the application filed under Order VII, Rule 11 of the said Code travelled beyond the averments of the application. According to settle maxim of law enunciated by our apex Court are that if it is apparent on the face of the record or on plain reading of the pleadings of the suit it appears that the suit is barred by any law or does not disclose any cause of action only in that case the plaint can be rejected. Here in this case admittedly a pre-emption case under section 96 of the said Act is a miscellaneous proceeding, it is not a suit. Therefore, there is nothing to reject on an application under Order vii Rule II of the said code as the same is not plaint rather, it is a miscellaneous proceeding arising out of a pre-emption claim under Section 96 of the said Act, and, as such, the Court below has committed error of law in rejecting the application under proceeding which is liable to be set-aside. 

 7. Heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner and considered his submissions. Perused the impugned order and annexure appended with the revisional application. On perusal of Annexure A, the application for pre-emption under Section 96 of the said Act being Miscellaneous Case No.129 of 2008, it appears that the statement made in the application of the miscellaneous case is neither barred by any law nor on the face of the record it appears that it does not disclose any cause of action to file the instant miscellaneous case. It further appears from the application for rejection of the plaint wherein the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 categorically stated some facts which were neither incorporated nor apparent on the face of the averment in the application for miscellaneous case. Rather, all the materials incorporated in the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the said Code are extraneous matter which cannot be considered as evidence and accepted on an application without taking any evidence. Apex Court has already decided and enunciated the maxim of law that in rejecting the plaint on an application filed under Order VII, rule 11 of the said Code the court cannot travel beyond the plaint and considered the extraneous matter. It will be noteworthy to quote the precedents to the case of Abul Khair vs Pubali Bank Ltd. reported in 53 DLR (AD) 62, wherein their Lordships held that. 

 10. More-so, we are of the firm view that the proceeding started under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not a suit, it is an application which does not come within the purview of the plaint according to Order VII, rule I of the Code. The plaint has been explained and codified in Order-VII of the said code. On the other hand, the application for pre-emption under section 96 of the Act is mere a proceeding which cannot be denoted as plaint within the ambit of Order VII, of the said Code although it has got all the Trappings of a plaint.
